title: The Boast (on the sea kit)
part: The sea kit on the Cyclops's shore
hypothesis: The taunt, the hurled peak and the curse read as a ship at sea under an angry giant if the water is a stepped brick ocean that moves and heaves the ship, the rocks' waves reach her, the weather gathers under the curse, and the men aboard sit and row on the ship rather than in it.
variable: look.sea on every key (a bright morning sea, the waves of the two rocks, the curse's cloud and wind; the sea lowered 7.6 plates to the baked water; benches under the five rowers); the seated rowers lifted 30 units onto them and the two forward rowers re-blocked. Same sheet, voice and cut; the shot plan re-solved (40 of 40 legal).

metrics_before.clip_before_fix: 80.8 s visible in 49 intervals (the keys re-shot on the sea kit before the rowers were lifted; feet in the deck, two rowers one inside the other)

metrics_after.clip: CLIP OD-B09-S11 visible 0.0 s in 0 intervals

checks.test: no one runs through anything: the rowers sit on thwarts, not in the deck; no man inside another; feet on the deck as she heaves
checks.note: tools/metis/clip.js on the take: 0 visible intervals (camera replay). Before the fix the same check found 80.8 s in 49 intervals: the five seated rowers' legs sunk 0.13 H into the deck (sat on it with the hips 1.5 units up) and two rowers seated one inside the other's back (both snapped to the same narrow place on the bow deck). Now each sits 30 units up on a brick thwart in the hull's frame (look.sea benches), and the two forward rowers have exact marks side by side (-88, 100) and (-48, 100)

checks.test: the ship rides the water and the rocks' waves reach her
checks.note: the sea lowered 7.6 plates to the baked water (the sea piece's top is the shore's); the swell rises from 0.6 to 1.15 as the peak lands (21.5 s) and to 1.2 at the second rock (97.7 s), the sheet's push toward the shore kept; the oars sweep on the rowing clocks (20-28 s, 95-100.5 s)

checks.test: the weather turns with the curse
checks.note: cloud plates, a darker sea and wind come up over K4 (47-55 s) under the key's dark sky while Polyphemus prays to Poseidon

result: Published as take 2. The ship heaves on a stepped sea under the shore, the rocks' waves reach her, the curse brings cloud and wind, and the crew sit on thwarts. Loose: the closes (most of the 40 shots) are faces with sea behind; the prop oars in the rowers' hands and the hull's cut oars are both drawn (two oars a man in some frames); the thwarts are plain brick columns; the curse's sky is the key's own, so it lightens again for the second rock.
